A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReVisiT research work. All 23 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable, and retained methods, figures, tables, and qualitative examples can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original CHAIR, POPE, AMBER, DeepSeekVL2, latency, ablation, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, vision-token diagnostic analyses, model-scaling experiments, ablations, latency measurements, and qualitative results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain adaptive vocabulary constraints, cached vision-token projections, minimum-JSD token/layer selection, and multiplicative output refinement. Notation and explanations change, but the proposed decoding procedure does not.

E1.justification: v2 removes AMBER evaluation and adds HallusionBench's visual-dependent original/edited-image questions, MMMU multidisciplinary reasoning, and VQAv2 open-ended question answering. CHAIR, POPE's three datasets and query types, and LLaVA-Bench qualitative examples remain. Coverage expands substantially beyond the earlier hallucination-focused evaluation.

E2.justification: CODE is added as an evaluated comparator in the retained CHAIR, POPE, and latency comparisons, alongside the unchanged Greedy, DoLa, VCD, M3ID, and SID comparator set. It also participates in the new benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: CHAIR reporting replaces Recall with mean per-caption F1. v2 adds five model configurations and removes the DeepSeekVL2 setting. New protocols include teacher-forced image-removal controls, GPT-4 judging on HallusionBench, and MMMU evaluation on 857 single-image items. The timing CPU changes from AMD EPYC 9354 to Intel Xeon Gold 5320. The retained CHAIR sample size/seed and POPE design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic analyses of grounded alternatives at hallucinated steps, image-present versus image-absent predictions, and constrained versus full-vocabulary vision-token projections (Section 2). It adds random and maximum-JSD selection controls and expands the reported threshold sweep from three to six values (Table 10). Earlier qualitative cases and vocabulary/layer ablations are retained or extended.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's latency means and standard deviations, v2 introduces 95% Wilson intervals and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Pratt handling and Holm-adjusted p-values for its diagnostic analyses (Appendix A.1). The existing CHAIR seed and latency practice of three decodes for each of 300 samples are retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark, diagnostic, scaling, and ablation results while removing AMBER and DeepSeekVL2 results. Retained scores also change: Qwen ReVisiT CHAIR_S/CHAIR_I become 29.8/7.04 instead of 31.6/7.56; POPE average accuracy changes from 84.77 to 84.53, now below SID's 85.78. These are revised reported results, not established method improvements. Latency values also change under a different reported CPU.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces formal definitions for at-least-one recall@k, single-token ground-truth/hallucinated-object subsets, and paired probability contrasts. These formalize the new diagnostics; the core decoding mathematics remains equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly extends the claimed benefits to general-purpose VQA and scalability across six model sizes spanning three architectures. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion foreground understanding vision-token information during hallucination. The earlier emphasis was efficient hallucination mitigation; the training-free decoding contribution and up-to-2x cost claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 refines the mechanism interpretation: visual input favors ground-truth objects overall, but the corresponding shift is not significant at hallucinated steps, where language priors can dominate. It also replaces the earlier threshold tradeoff discussion with a modest-sensitivity interpretation. Existing limitations concerning visually salient cues and unavailable external knowledge are retained in Appendix D.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly discloses top-p, top-k, and beam settings, diagnostic tokenization/alignment rules, HallusionBench judge inputs, and MMMU filtering and prompt instructions. Timing hardware information is revised, while AMBER resizing and DeepSeek repetition-penalty details disappear with those experiments. ReVisiT pseudocode, caching instructions, hyperparameter guidance, and code access remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The pre-/intra-/post-alignment taxonomy and detailed related-work discussion are retained in Appendix A.3. v2 adds vision-representation interpretation and retrieval-augmented-generation references, CODE, and new benchmark/model citations, while dropping several early-exit and removed-evaluation references. This refines positioning without replacing the established relationship to prior decoding approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation, experimental discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Preliminary notation moves into Section 3; related work, the main qualitative discussion, and limitations move into appendices. The narrative shifts from prior-method motivation toward empirical investigation of vision tokens, beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds model-scaling and diagnostic plots, new benchmark/statistical tables, and an ablation plot with an expanded two-panel table. The retained overview becomes Figure 5, and the cartoon example moves from main-text Figure 4 to appendix Figure 9. The document template, headers, captions, table structures, and placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly motivates its central design through illustrative examples and does not test minimum-JSD selection against random or maximum-JSD alternatives. v2 addresses these important evidence gaps through controlled vision-token analyses with statistical reporting and direct selection ablations (Section 2, Appendices A.1 and B.2). General VQA and model-scaling evaluations further strengthen applicability evidence. Although AMBER/MoE evidence is lost and some existing score revisions remain unexplained, the substantially stronger support for the method's rationale and scope outweighs these costs.
